title: Cost it, price it, sell it honestly, then plan ahead
course_title: Natural Skincare: Basic Creams, Lotions and Facial Oils

say: Cost it, price it, sell it honestly, then plan ahead.
This is the video for module four of Natural Skincare.
Creams look cheap to make, because most of the jar is water. But emulsifying wax, preservative, packaging, labels, labour and laboratory tests add up quickly.

panel.heading: Mostly water does not mean cheap
items: Wax, preservative and jars add up
Labour and testing are real costs

say: Many new makers copy other people's prices, and only later discover they lose money on every jar. The naira prices in this video are approximate examples for practice only. Use the prices on your own receipts.

panel.heading: Mostly water does not mean cheap
items: Wax, preservative and jars add up
Labour and testing are real costs

say: Start with cost per gram. Divide what you paid by the grams you received. If 500 g of emulsifying wax cost 8,000 naira, that is 16 naira a gram.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: Rukayat multiplies every ingredient in her 265 g batch by its cost per gram. The ingredients total 836 naira.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: Then five jars with lids at 400 each, 2,000. Labels, 500. Gas, 300, and gloves and alcohol, 300.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: Her own labour, 2 hours at 1,500 an hour, is 3,000. And she sets aside 150 a jar towards laboratory tests, 750.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: The batch total is 7,686 naira, so each jar costs about 1,540. The ingredients were only about 170 a jar. Pricing at 1,000 because it is mostly water would lose money.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: For a 40 percent margin, divide the cost by 0.6. 1,540 divided by 0.6 is 2,567, which she rounds to 2,600 naira. Then she checks what similar creams sell for nearby.

panel.heading: Rukayat costs five jars of cream
items: Cost per gram: 8,000 ÷ 500 g = 16 a gram

say: Facial oils are the opposite of creams. There is no water, so the oils are the biggest cost.
Jojoba at 90 naira a gram comes to 1,215. Baobab, 486.
Rosehip, 421, and vitamin E, 22.
The oils total about 2,145 naira. Add the amber bottle, label, sanitiser, half an hour of labour and testing, and the bottle costs about 3,895. At a 40 percent margin, the price is about 6,500 naira.
If your price is far higher than others, look for safe savings. Buy jars and wax in bulk once your formula passes stability tests, and make larger batches so labour per jar falls.
And count failed batches. If one batch in ten is lost, that adds about 10 percent to your cost.

panel.heading: Where to save, where never to
left: Buy jars and wax in bulk

say: But never save money by cutting the preservative, skipping pH checks, or using tap water.

panel.heading: Where to save, where never to
left: Buy jars and wax in bulk

say: Answer questions honestly. If a customer asks whether it will lighten her skin, say no. It is a moisturiser that keeps skin soft. If you have not formulated or tested it for babies, say you cannot recommend it for them.

cards.d: Will it lighten my skin? No, it is a moisturiser. Not tested for babies, so not recommended.
Only from preserved, tested batches, in labelled pots. No fingers in display testers.
Check the money arrived in your bank or wallet app before handing over. Screenshots can be faked.

say: Give samples only from preserved, stability-tested batches, in sanitised, labelled pots. Never sell cream scooped into unlabelled nylon or reused containers.

cards.d: Will it lighten my skin? No, it is a moisturiser. Not tested for babies, so not recommended.
Only from preserved, tested batches, in labelled pots. No fingers in display testers.

say: Confirm each order in writing on WhatsApp. Then check the money has actually arrived in your Moniepoint, Opay or bank app before you hand over goods, because payment screenshots can be faked.

say: Your project is a product file: formula, data sheets, batch record, stability log, feedback, label and costing, plus an honest reflection. For example, Ifeoma in Onitsha has a lotion that passed 8 weeks of stability checks, and a facial oil that passed 12.

panel.heading: Ifeoma's 90-day plan
items: Days 15 to 30: sell oil to 10 customers
Days 61 to 75: get lab test quotes
Days 76 to 90: CAC and NAFDAC steps

say: In days 1 to 14 she continues the lotion test to week 12. In days 15 to 30 she sells the facial oil to 10 existing customers at 6,500 naira, and gives 5 labelled lotion samples for feedback.

say: If 3 or more say the lotion is too thin, she makes version 1.1 with 2 percent more shea and 2 percent less water, and starts a new stability test.

say: Then she asks two laboratories for test quotes, and lists her CAC and NAFDAC documents. Selling the lotion widely waits for the testing that makes it safe.

say: To remember. Count packaging, labour and testing, not just ingredients. Price by dividing cost by one minus your margin. Never cut safety to cut cost.
Answer honestly, sample cleanly, and confirm every payment in your own app.
